title: On the coefficient formula for de Branges-Rovnyak norms
summary: Let $\mathcal{H}(b)$ be the de Branges-Rovnyak space associated to a non-extreme point $b$ of the unit ball of $H^\infty$, and let $φ=b/a$, where $a$ is the Pythagorean mate of $b$. It is known that, if $f$ is a function holomorphic on a neighbourhood of the closed unit disk, then it belongs to $\mathcal{H}(b)$, and its norm in $\mathcal{H}(b)$ can be expressed in terms of the Taylor coefficients of $f$ and $φ$ via the formula \[ \|f\|_{\mathcal{H}(b)}^2=\sum_{m\ge0}|\hat{f}(m)|^2 +\sum_{m\ge0}\Bigl|\sum_{n\ge0}\overline{\hatφ(n)}\hat{f}(m+n)\Bigr|^2. \] However, the formula can break down…
